task.title: Find a person
task.shortdesc: Search your tree by a name, a place or an event, then open the person you want.

context.p: The search box is on . It searches the tree that is open.

stepresult.p: The name of your tree shows, with a search box under it.

step.cmd: Type a name, a place or an event in the search box.

stepresult.p: The results come in two lists side by side. The people come first. The events come next to them. A card shows a person's name and years. A chip on it says how many sources back that person up.
A line such as Matched: Patrick says what the search found. An event is named for what happened and who it was about, such as Marriage — Patrick Brontë & Maria Branwell.

step.cmd: Choose the card of the person you want.

stepresult.p: The page of that person opens. Their name shows in the chip that starts with .

result.p: Now , and in the menu all show that person.

postreq.p: To see everyone, choose on . After you have opened someone, also has two headings. Under is a button with the name of the person you opened last. Under is a button for each person you opened lately.

To narrow the results, choose the button with a small icon and no words, next to . A panel with the heading opens. Select , , or to add a filter. Select to also find names that sound alike. Choose to start again.
